question: A box contains 6 red, 5 white and 4 black balls. Three balls are drawn successively without replacement. Determine the probability that the three balls drawn are of three different colours, using the multiplication theorem on probability.
explanation:
Given Information
There are $6+5+4=15$ balls. For three balls to be of different colours, exactly one red, one white and one black ball must be drawn. These colours can occur in $3!=6$ different orders.

Consider the particular order red, white, black. By the multiplication theorem on probability,
$$P(RWB)=P(R)P(W|R)P(B|R\cap W).$$
Now,
$$P(R)=\frac{6}{15},\qquad P(W|R)=\frac{5}{14},\qquad P(B|R\cap W)=\frac{4}{13}.$$
Therefore,
$$P(RWB)=\frac{6}{15}\times\frac{5}{14}\times\frac{4}{13}=\frac{4}{91}.$$

The numerator for every other order of one red, one white and one black ball is also $6\times5\times4$, while the successive denominators remain $15,14,13$. Hence each of the six possible colour orders has probability $\frac{4}{91}$. Since these six orders are mutually exclusive,
$$P(\text{three different colours})=6\times\frac{4}{91}=\frac{24}{91}.$$

Final Result
Therefore, the probability that the three balls drawn are of three different colours is $\frac{24}{91}$.
